subject.title: [Bug]: default memory hook blocks repeated channel restart recovery

question: Should OpenClaw add a typed, host-enforced trigger/activation scope to plugin hook registrations so restart recovery can safely ignore hooks guaranteed not to run for recovered user turns?
rationale: The fix changes the plugin hook contract and restart-safety boundary; source inspection supports the need for a host-owned distinction but cannot choose the permanent public API shape.

options.title: Add host-enforced hook scope
options.body: Introduce a typed registration contract that the host validates before restart recovery skips an otherwise globally registered hook.

options.title: Keep universal hook blocking
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed behavior and accept resend recovery whenever any `before_agent_reply` hook is registered.

options.title: Redesign the memory hook seam
options.body: Move the default memory behavior to a narrower existing lifecycle hook if it can preserve heartbeat and cron semantics without expanding the claiming-hook API.

recommendation.title: Add host-enforced hook scope
recommendation.body: Introduce a typed registration contract that the host validates before restart recovery skips an otherwise globally registered hook.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant merged restart-recovery and multi-restart QA work links this contributor directly to the affected behavior and validation scenario.
